question.problem:
Find the smallest natural number solution to the system of linear congruences below.

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x≡2 & (\text{mod}\,3) \\ x≡4 & (\text{mod}\,7) \\ x≡5 & (\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since $3,$ $7,$ and $8$ are coprime, then according to the Chinese remainder theorem, the system has a unique solution modulo $3\cdot 7\cdot 8=168.$

We will solve the system in two steps.

**Step 1.** Find the common solution for the first and second congruences of the system.

From the first congruence, we get

$$
x≡2\,(\text{mod}\,3)\,⟹\,x=2+3t,\,t\in Z.
$$

Substituting this into the second congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡4 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,7) \\ 2+3t & ≡4 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,7) \\ 3t & ≡2 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,7)\end{aligned}
$$

Since $7$ is a relatively small modulus, we can solve it by trial and error. We have that $5\cdot 3≡1\,(\text{mod}\,7).$ So, we multiply both sides by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3t & ≡2 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,7) \\ 5\cdot 3t & ≡10 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,7) \\ t & ≡3 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,7)\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $t=3+7s,$ where $s\in Z.$ Substituting this into the expression for $x,$ we get the common solution for the first and second congruences:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2+3t \\  & =2+3(3+7s) \\  & =11+21s\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2.** Find the common solution of all three congruences.

Now, substituting the common solution of the first two congruences into the third congruence, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ≡5 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,8) \\ 11+21s & ≡5 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,8) \\ 21s & ≡-6 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,8) \\ 5s & ≡2 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

Since $8$ is a relatively small modulus, by trial and error, we have that $5\cdot 5≡1\,(\text{mod}\,8).$ So, we multiply both sides by $5:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5s & ≡2 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,8) \\ 5\cdot 5s & ≡10 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,8) \\ s & ≡2 &  & \,(\text{mod}\,8)\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $s=2+8u,$ where $u\in Z.$ Substituting this into the expression for the common solution of the first two congruences, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =11+21s \\  & =11+21(2+8u) \\  & =53+168u.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $x≡53\,(\text{mod}\,168)$ is the unique solution modulo $168,$ and $x=53$ is the smallest natural number solution to the system.
